cards.front: What type does Math.pow take and return?
cards.back: It takes two doubles and returns a double
cards.extra: Even Math.pow(2, 3) returns 8.0. Cast or use a loop if you need integer results.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.front: What do Math.max, Math.min and Math.abs do?
cards.back: Return the larger, the smaller, or the absolute value of their arguments
cards.extra: They are overloaded for int, long, float and double; the return type follows the argument type.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.front: What range does Math.random() return?
cards.back: 0.0 (inclusive) to 1.0 (exclusive)
cards.extra: So a die is (int)(Math.random() * 6) + 1 — multiply to widen the range, add to shift it.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.front: What does Integer.parseInt do, and what can go wrong?
cards.back: Converts a String to an int; throws NumberFormatException if it is not a number
cards.extra: It does not trim or tolerate spaces, and it fails on overflow — "12a" throws rather than returning null.
cards.source: YouTube — parseInt Java Tutorial - String to Integer, 0:01 (youtu.be/Pnaqn6GOyzU?t=1)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::03 Data Types

cards.front: What does casting a double to an int do?
cards.back: Truncates the fractional part — it does not round
cards.extra: (int) 9.9 is 9, not 10. Use Math.round when you want rounding.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::03 Data Types

cards.front: When is a cast required?
cards.back: Only for narrowing conversions — the compiler will not silently lose information
cards.extra: Widening (int to double) is automatic; narrowing back needs the explicit cast, which can lose precision.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::03 Data Types

cards.front: What is the ternary operator's shape?
cards.back: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse
cards.extra: It is an expression, not a statement, so it can be assigned. Both branches must produce a compatible type.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::04 Conditionals

cards.front: What two classes does the video use to read a text file?
cards.back: File plus Scanner (or BufferedReader)
cards.extra: Both need closing; try-with-resources is the modern way to guarantee it.
cards.source: YouTube — Files In Java - Read Text File Easily, 0:00 (youtu.be/lHFlAYaNfdo?t=0)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: How do you read a CSV file into an array?
cards.back: line.split(",") per line, into String[]
cards.extra: The split is on the literal comma — quoted fields containing commas break it, which is why real CSV needs a parser.
cards.source: YouTube — Java: Read a CSV File into an Array, 0:01 (youtu.be/-Aud0cDh-J8?t=1)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: Which classes does the video use for dates and formatting?
cards.back: Date with SimpleDateFormat
cards.extra: Both are legacy; the modern API is LocalDate/LocalDateTime with DateTimeFormatter. Format patterns are strings like "dd/MM/yyyy".
cards.source: YouTube — Java Date and Time Tutorial, 1:05 (youtu.be/6cp4P4XZ9hE?t=65)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: What does instanceof test?
cards.back: Whether an object is an instance of a class or implements an interface, at runtime
cards.extra: It returns false for null rather than throwing, which makes it a safe type test before a cast.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Polymorphism

cards.front: Where must super() appear in a constructor?
cards.back: First statement, or the compiler inserts a no-argument super() for you
cards.extra: If the superclass has no no-arg constructor, the subclass will not compile until it calls one explicitly.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::12 Inheritance

cards.front: What does this refer to, and what is its most common use?
cards.back: The current object; used to tell a field apart from a parameter of the same name
cards.extra: this.name = name; — left side is the field, right side the parameter.
cards.source: YouTube — This Keyword in Java Tutorial, 0:00 (youtu.be/CSWrefLneXE?t=0)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What is encapsulation in practice?
cards.back: Private fields with public getters/setters that control access
cards.extra: The point is not the getters but the control: validation, computed values, and the freedom to change storage later.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: How does method chaining work?
cards.back: Each method returns this, so the next call can be appended
cards.extra: b.setX(1).setY(2); — the pattern behind builders and fluent APIs.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What keyword does a class use to take on an interface?
cards.back: implements — a class extends a class but implements an interface
cards.extra: A class may implement many interfaces but extend only one class, which is how Java gets multiple inheritance of type without the diamond problem.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::16 Interfaces

cards.front: What can an abstract class do that an interface could not (pre-Java 8)?
cards.back: Declare state — fields and constructors — that subclasses share
cards.extra: It also cannot be instantiated. Interfaces carry no instance fields.
cards.source: YouTube — Abstract Class In Java Tutorial, 0:01 (youtu.be/52frlN8webg?t=1)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::11 Abstraction

cards.front: What does final mean in its three positions?
cards.back: Variable: cannot be reassigned. Method: cannot be overridden. Class: cannot be subclassed
cards.extra: For a reference variable it freezes the reference, not the object it points to.
cards.source: YouTube — Final Keyword In Java Tutorial, 0:01 (youtu.be/730BMKm4qYM?t=1)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::12 Inheritance

cards.front: What are Java's four access levels, from most to least open?
cards.back: public, protected, package-private (no keyword), private
cards.extra: protected means package plus subclasses; the missing keyword is a real level, not a typo.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::03 Access Modifiers

cards.front: When does the compiler stop giving you a default constructor?
cards.back: As soon as you declare any constructor yourself
cards.extra: Then new Foo() fails unless you add a no-arg constructor back.
cards.source: YouTube — Java Constructor Tutorial - How To Use A Constructor in Java, 0:00 (youtu.be/G1Iln3PSrUg?t=0)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: Why can a static method not use instance fields?
cards.back: It runs with no object, so there is no this to read a field from
cards.extra: Static members belong to the class; access them as ClassName.member.
cards.source: YouTube — Static Method In Java Tutorial, 0:03 (youtu.be/xKZ3sMimQYM?t=3)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What happens in a switch when a case has no break?
cards.back: Fall-through — execution continues into the next case
cards.extra: Usually a bug, occasionally deliberate (grouped cases). Modern code uses arrow cases, which do not fall through.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::04 Conditionals
